answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not next week, and not 40 miles yet. Your heart rate and pace are back to normal, but quads and calves that carried you through a 3:50 marathon usually lag behind how the engine feels. Going from 12 miles to 40 is more than triple, and speedwork loads those muscles harder than easy running does.

You still have time to be ready for the 10K. Here is a rough ramp if you race it, and I will adjust it from how each week goes.

| Week | Miles | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | about 19 | Easy runs, a few short strides |
| Nov 2 – 8 | 24 – 26 | Five easy days, strides twice |
| Nov 9 – 15 | 30 – 32 | First short 10K-pace session |
| Nov 16 – 22 | 34 – 36 | One sharpening session, one longer easy run |

The week of the race itself would taper from there, wherever the Thanksgiving 10K falls. So, are you racing it, or would you rather rebuild base first? Tell me which and I will shape the weeks around your answer.

new.analysis:
You followed last week exactly. All three easy runs were done at 3, 4 and 5 miles, nothing was skipped, nothing was overrun, and pain stayed at 0/10. Zero time above zone 2 was the right way to spend the first week after a marathon.

Your numbers came back fast. Easy pace went from 10:49 at heart rate 128 on Wednesday to 9:51 at 139 on Sunday, which is where you were before the race. That is a good sign for your aerobic system, but muscle and tendon recovery runs slower than heart rate does. Feeling ready is the normal trap at this point, and it is the reason to build in steps.

The race itself was a big load: nearly four hours at an average heart rate of 161, about 86% of your max, after weeks of 40-plus miles. Your quads and calves took most of it. A second easy week with a few more runs lets them rebuild without asking for speed.

This week uses four runs rather than five. Wednesday becomes strength so you never run on back-to-back days while the legs are still repairing. The strides on Saturday are a check on turnover, not a workout, and you can drop them if the legs feel flat.

Your answer on the 10K changes what comes after this week. If you race it, short faster work starts the week of Nov 9 and the build stays modest. If you skip it, I would keep adding easy volume and strides for several more weeks before any structured sessions. Either way the next block starts from a rested base, not from a rush back to 40.
